analysis:
I examined head lines 588-1779 of provider-swift/Sources/ProviderCore/Server/StandaloneServer.swift. These cover the stop/finishShutdown lifecycle, native MiMo and GLM retirement guards, KV reslice and build with restore-on-throw, LRU eviction, memory headroom, acquireModel reservation, computeStandaloneWeightHash (1743-1754) and the start of ensureModelLoaded. None of these lines fall inside the PR's changed ranges (head 1964-1969 and 1999-2006; the range map is complete), so they serve as context only. I found no regression in them.

The actual change, seen only in a truncated patch excerpt, is in the standalone load path. For managed GLM5Next loads it drops both the pre-load and post-load computeStandaloneWeightHash passes. It also removes the explicit identityMismatch check against glmPlan.weights.manifest.aggregateSHA256. In their place it relies on the managed load's own per-file SHA-256 manifest verification. glmPlan.weights.recheck() is still called, and preLoadArtifactHash became a var, which presumably gets assigned the verified digest later.

The next pass must verify the following:
(1) The glmLoad / loadServingContainer path hashes the exact bytes it maps or loads, rather than hashing first and re-reading afterwards. This is a weight-substitution TOCTOU by the operator (ADV-001, T-012, T-027, A-004). The removed post-load hash was the bracket that closed that window.
(2) postLoadArtifactHash (head ~1999-2006, not visible here) is set only from the verified manifest digest. It must fail closed (throw) when verification is missing or mismatched, and must never be left nil or set to a fallback value.
(3) The cacheEligibleWeightHash / modelArtifactSHA256 handed to resliceAndBuildSlot (lines 1128-1143, 1271-1299) is still a verified hash. The SSD prefix-cache weightHash binding in T-041 depends on this, and a stale or unverified value could bind cache entries to the wrong weights.

Because the changed lines are not in these units, I recorded no findings and am requesting deeper review.
